title: Projective cofibrancy of coherent join-cone weights
statement:
Fix universes and small simplicial sets as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and use the subset-poset coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set, let $A=\mathfrak C[K]$, and let $b$ and $t$ denote the new vertices of $\Delta^0\star K$ and $K\star\Delta^0$, respectively. Composition defines enriched functors
$$W^-_K:A\longrightarrow\mathsf{sSet},\qquad W^-_K(a)=\mathfrak C[\Delta^0\star K](b,a),$$
$$W^+_K:A^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\mathsf{sSet},\qquad W^+_K(a)=\mathfrak C[K\star\Delta^0](a,t).$$
Both weights are projectively cofibrant in the following explicit sense. For $B=A$ and $W=W^-_K$, or $B=A^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $W=W^+_K$, the map $\varnothing\to W$ in enriched functors $B\to\mathsf{sSet}$ is a retract of a transfinite composite, continuous at limit stages, of pushouts of coproducts of the free boundary maps
$$B(a,-)\times\partial\Delta^r\longrightarrow B(a,-)\times\Delta^r,\qquad a\in\operatorname{Ob}(B),\quad r\geq0.$$
Here $\partial\Delta^r$ is the union of the proper faces of $\Delta^r$, $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$, and all functor colimits and products with simplicial sets are computed at each object. No Kan condition on $A$ or finiteness condition on $K$ is imposed.

source.place: Riehl–Verity, Recognizing quasi-categorical limits and colimits in homotopy coherent nerves, Definition 5.2.8 and Lemma 5.2.9, printed p.34, using Theorem 5.2.6, pp.32–34. The right-cone version is the opposite of the left-cone version. Read the authors’ online PDF; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched result.

proof.text: Put $X=\Delta^0\amalg K$ and $Y=\Delta^0\star K$. The ordered join described in [lem-coef-join-boundary-cubical-extension] makes $X\hookrightarrow Y$ degreewise injective and bijective on vertices. Its coherent realization has source $D_0=\mathbf1\amalg A$: a functor out of the defining simplex colimit on a disjoint union is precisely a pair of functors on the two factors, and $\mathfrak C[\Delta^0]=\mathbf1$. Apply [lem-coef-coherent-realization-relative-cells] to obtain a sequence of subcategories $D_j\subseteq D=\mathfrak C[Y]$ with this initial stage, constant object set, colimit $D$, and only cells $U(\partial\Delta^r)\to U(\Delta^r)$.

source.place: Definitions 5.1.8 and 5.2.8, Lemma 5.1.9; start of Lemma 5.2.9

proof.text: By [lem-coef-join-boundary-cubical-extension], $D$ restricts to exactly $A$ on its old objects, has $D(b,b)=\Delta^0$, and has no arrows from an old object to $b$. Since $D_0\subseteq D_j\subseteq D$, these same assertions hold at every stage. The only mapping sets that can grow are $D_j(b,a)$. Define $V_j(a)=D_j(b,a)$ with the action given by composition in $D_j$. The unit and associativity equations are the enriched functor equations, so $V_j:A\to\mathsf{sSet}$ is a weight, $V_0=\varnothing$, and $D_j$ is exactly the category with old full subcategory $A$, one new source $b$, and outgoing weight $V_j$. Every cell has endpoints $(b,a)$: its new top simplex cannot lie in any of the other mapping sets, all of which are already completely contained in $D_0$.

source.place: Definition 5.2.2 and converse direction of Theorem 5.2.6, pp.31–34

proof.text: For a cell of dimension $r$ ending at $a$, let $u:\partial\Delta^r\to V_j(a)$ be its attaching boundary. Define an action-compatible map $A(a,-)\times\partial\Delta^r\to V_j$ by $(f,z)\mapsto f\circ u(z)$. Let $P$ be the pushout of the coproduct of these maps along $A(a,-)\times\partial\Delta^r\hookrightarrow A(a,-)\times\Delta^r$, over all cells at stage $j$. These functor pushouts are computed objectwise: composition acts on each representative, and the imposed relations are action-compatible; products with a fixed simplicial set preserve these quotient colimits degreewise, since the inverse is represented using the same fixed coordinate. Thus the objectwise pushout has an enriched action and the required functor pushout property.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.6, square (5.2.7); explicit free-weight attaching maps

proof.text: The category with old part $A$, new source $b$ and outgoing weight $P$ is precisely the simplicial-category pushout defining $D_{j+1}$. To check this, fix any target simplicial category $E$, a functor on $D_j$, and the images of all the existing objects. Extending across a cell with endpoints $(b,a)$ means choosing $h:\Delta^r\to E(Fb,Fa)$ extending $F(u)$. A natural map from $A(a,-)\times\Delta^r$ to $E(Fb,F(-))$ is determined by this $h$: its value at $(f,z)$ must be $F(f)\circ h(z)$, and conversely that formula is natural and recovers $h$ at $(1_a,z)$. Agreement on the boundary is exactly the pushout relation. The choices for the coproduct of cells are independent. These mutually inverse descriptions prove the universal property and identify $V_{j+1}=P$, including the old-weight maps. Hence every $V_j\to V_{j+1}$ is a pushout of the required free boundary maps.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.2.6, universal property of (5.2.7), written out rather than assuming a mapping-set functor preserves colimits

proof.text: Put $V_\omega=\operatorname{colim}_{j<\omega}V_j$ objectwise. Its category with old part $A$ and new source $b$ is the colimit of the $D_j$: a functor out of it is a functor on $A$, an image for $b$, and an action-compatible map from $V_\omega$, equivalently compatible such maps from every $V_j$. Thus $V_\omega(a)=D(b,a)=W^-_K(a)$ with its specified action. The sequence, extended at the limit ordinal $\omega$ by this colimit, is continuous. It actually presents $\varnothing\to W^-_K$ as a free boundary cell composite; the identity retraction gives the weaker retract assertion in the statement. All cell-index sets are small because the realization categories in the cited presentation are small.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.6, concluding colimit argument, and Lemma 5.2.9

proof.text: For the right weight apply [lem-coef-coherent-realization-relative-cells] instead to $K\amalg\Delta^0\hookrightarrow K\star\Delta^0$, again a vertex-bijective injection. By [lem-coef-join-boundary-cubical-extension] its final category has full old part $A$, point endomorphisms at $t$, and no maps from $t$ to $A$. Reverse all arrows of this sequence of simplicial categories. Taking opposites is an involutive equivalence of their ordinary category, so it preserves each pushout and the sequential colimit by their mapping-out properties. Moreover $U(T)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong U(T)$ by interchanging its two object labels; this isomorphism commutes with every map of $T$, so it preserves the boundary-cell shape without reversing simplicial operators. The reversed sequence starts at $\mathbf1\amalg A^{\mathrm{op}}$, has new source $t$, and its outgoing weight is exactly $a\mapsto\mathfrak C[K\star\Delta^0](a,t)$ with action by precomposition. Steps 2–5 therefore apply with $B=A^{\mathrm{op}}$ and give the stated cells $B(a,-)\times\partial\Delta^r\to B(a,-)\times\Delta^r$. If $K=\varnothing$, there are no old objects or cells and both weights are the unique empty diagram; $r=0$ simply attaches free vertex cells since its boundary is empty.

source.place: Right-cone dual of Definitions 5.2.8 and Lemma 5.2.9; opposite of the cellular proof, not a model-category classification theorem

proof_origin.place: Online Riehl–Verity, §§5.1–5.2, especially the converse proof of Theorem 5.2.6 and Lemma 5.2.9; archival copy WANTED. The explicit pushout comparison and opposite argument are written out.

split_report.summary: One new general coherent-realization cellular-presentation lemma. Reused the existing coherent-join full-subcategory calculation, and proved the passage from simplicial-category mapping cells to free weight cells by explicit universal properties. Applied ordinary simplicial-category opposites for the right cone, without imposing local Kan or finite hypotheses. Read Riehl–Verity online, checked sources, all citation statements, the whole DAG and blueprint, and both project sources. No exact attachment or Mathlib match exists. The printed final join in the proof of Lemma 5.2.9 is a typographical reversal; its Definition 5.2.8 fixes the intended left join.
